subject: geography
topicName: Economic Development in LICs and NEEs

steps.title: Key Facts
steps.body: Nigeria is located in West Africa with a population of over 220 million (2023), making it Africa's most populous country. Its GNI per head is approximately $2,160 (2022), classifying it as an NEE. Nigeria has the largest economy in Africa, with a GDP of over $440 billion.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Nigeria's industrial structure has changed significantly. The economy has shifted from a primary-sector-dominated economy to one with a growing secondary and tertiary sector. However, it remains heavily dependent on oil.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Transnational Corporations (TNCs) are companies that operate in more than one country. They play a major role in Nigeria's economy, particularly in the oil and telecommunications sectors.

steps.title: Limitations of Aid in Nigeria
steps.body: Aid effectiveness is reduced by corruption - Nigeria ranks 150th out of 180 on Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index (2022). Boko Haram's insurgency in the northeast has displaced over 2 million people and disrupted aid delivery. Some argue that aid creates dependency rather than building self-sufficiency.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how Nigeria's industrial structure has changed since the 1960s. | Explain the role of TNCs in Nigeria's economic development. Use the example of Shell. | Assess the environmental impacts of economic development in Nigeria.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use Nigeria as your named case study for LIC/NEE economic development questions Include specific data (percentages, years, figures) - examiners reward factual accuracy Always consider both positive and negative impacts of TNCs For environmental impacts, focus on the Niger Delta oil pollution with specific examples Remember to discuss inequality within Nigeria (north-south divide) as well as overall changes Higher mark questions: evaluate whether development has truly improved quality of life for all Link environmental impacts to specific groups affected (e.g. Ogoni people, fishermen)
